deep.reconstruction:
WHAT THE PAGE IS. For each prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) between about 1129 and 1481, in descending order and continuing the previous and next folios, Gauss writes down the cycles (periods) of reduced binary quadratic forms of positive determinant D = p. These are forms (a,b,c) = ax^2+2bxy+cy^2 with b^2 - ac = p, in the sense of Disquisitiones Arithmeticae art. 183-187. Each row lists the absolute values |a| of the successive first coefficients around one period.

The principal row. The row beginning with 1 is the principal cycle. Its entries are the denominators Q_k of the continued fraction of sqrt(p), produced by the recursion
- P_0 = 0, Q_0 = 1, a_k = floor((floor(sqrt p) + P_k)/Q_k),
- P_{k+1} = a_k Q_k - P_k,
- Q_{k+1} = (p - P_{k+1}^2)/Q_k.
Gauss stops at the first repeated value (e.g. '35.35 &c'). That repetition is the centre of symmetry of the period, so only half the period needs writing. The period length is odd because the fundamental unit has norm -1.

Example, p = 1229 (floor sqrt = 35):
- Q_1 = 1229 - 35^2 = 4;
- a_1 = 17, P_2 = 33, Q_2 = (1229 - 33^2)/4 = 35;
- a_2 = 1, P_3 = 2, Q_3 = (1229 - 4)/35 = 35.
This gives '1.4.35.35 &c', exactly as written.

Other principal rows checked by me the same way: 1481 (1, 37, 5, 65, 8, 49, ...), 1453 (1, 9, 33, ...), 1433 (1, 64, 11, ...), 1129 (1, 40, 27, 27) and 1289 (1, 64, ...). All agree.

The non-principal rows. Further rows begin with a small number m with p a quadratic residue mod m (3, 4, 5, 7, 9, ...). Each is the cycle of a non-principal class, written until it returns to m ('5.28. ... .41.5 &c'). A class and its inverse have mutually reversed cycles, so only one of each pair is written. The number of rows is therefore (h+1)/2, where h is the number of properly primitive classes of determinant p. The next folio's summary ('Inter 1000 & 2000 ...: 51 with h = 1, 9 with h = 3, 2 with h = 5, ...') confirms this:
- h = 3: 1373, 1301, 1229, 1213 (2 rows each);
- h = 5: 1429 (3 rows);
- h = 9: 1129 (5 rows);
- h = 11: 1297 (6 rows).

My check of the 1129 row '5.8.21.5'. Start from (5,33,-8): 33^2 + 40 = 1129. Reduction gives
(5,33,-8) -> (-8,31,21) -> (21,32,-5) -> (-5,33,8) -> (8,31,-21) -> (-21,32,5).
The absolute values are 5, 8, 21, 5. Starting instead from (5,32,-21) gives the reversed cycle 5, 21, 8, i.e. the inverse class.

My check of all cycles labelled '1296' (really determinant 1297 = 36^2 + 1, where sqrt(1297) = [36; 72-bar] gives the principal row '1.1'). Each cycle closes as written:
- (3,35,-24) -> (-24,13,47) -> (47,34,-3) gives 3, 24, 47, 3;
- (27,28,-19) -> (-19,29,24) -> (24,19,-39) -> (-39,20,23) -> (23,26,-27) gives 27, 19, 24, 39, 23, 27;
- (16,33,-13) -> (-13,32,21) -> (21,31,-16) gives 16, 13, 21, 16;
- (32,25,-21) -> (-21,17,48) -> (48,31,-7) -> (-7,32,39) -> (39,7,-32) gives 32, 21, 48, 7, 39, 32.

The marginal labels (group structure). For 1297 and 1129 Gauss adds margin labels 0.11, 1.10, 2.9, 3.8, 4.7, 5.6 and 0.9, 1.8, 2.7, 3.6, 4.5. These assign each listed cycle the pair of exponents {k, h-k} of a class C^k and its inverse in a cyclic class group of order h.
- For 1297 the generator is the class with first coefficient 3; its successive powers lead to the rows starting 9, 27, 16, 32.
- For 1129 the generator is the class with first coefficient 5, with powers giving the rows starting 25, 3, 7.
The label '3.6' on the 1129 row starting with 3 asserts that the cube of the 5-class is non-principal. That means the group is cyclic C9, not C3 x C3. I have not verified this by composition here.

Other marks. The circled '10' is the folio number. The '23.7.' in the bottom-left corner is unexplained; compare '22.3' on the previous folio. It is possibly a date.
errors: The determinant heading the 11-class table is written '1296' (as it appears in the image), but the cycles are those of determinant 1297 = 36^2+1 (principal cycle '1.1'; the next folio's summary lists 1297 with 11 classes). This is a slip of the pen, or the 6 is a malformed 7.
1433: a stray crossed-out figure appears after '37.37' before '&c'; it is a deleted false start, not part of the cycle.
No arithmetic errors were found in the sampled cycles: principal cycles of 1481, 1453, 1433, 1229, 1129, 1289, and all six cycles for 1297 and the 5-cycle for 1129 were recomputed and agree.

results.what: Principal periods of reduced forms of determinant p, i.e. the denominators Q_k of the continued fraction of sqrt(p), written as half-periods up to the symmetric repetition, for primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 from 1129 to 1481.
results.modern_name: Continued fraction expansion of sqrt(p) / principal cycle of reduced indefinite forms (infrastructure of the principal ideal class)
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange and Legendre for the continued fraction method; Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801, art. 183-187) for cycles of reduced forms

results.what: Complete enumeration of the non-principal cycles of reduced forms (one per inverse pair) for each p, yielding the class number h of properly primitive forms of determinant p (h = 3 for 1229, 1213, 1301, 1373; 5 for 1429; 9 for 1129; 11 for 1297).
results.modern_name: Class number tables for real quadratic orders Z[sqrt p] (discriminant 4p)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss; his tables of class numbers for positive determinants are printed in Werke II (Nachlass)

results.what: Marginal exponent labels k.(h-k) identifying the class group of determinant 1129 as cyclic of order 9 (generated by the class with a=5) and of 1297 as cyclic of order 11 (generated by a=3), with each cycle assigned to a power of the generator.
results.modern_name: Determination of the structure of the form class group, with explicit generator and discrete-log labelling of classes
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae art. 305-307 discuss cyclicity and generators of the class group; Nachlass tables)

deep.surprise_reason: These are Gauss's well-known class-number computations for positive prime determinants, exactly in the style of Disquisitiones art. 183-187 and of the tables published from his Nachlass in Werke II. Identifying cyclic group structure (C9 for 1129) is a nice detail but is in line with known Disquisitiones material on class-group structure.

checkable.asserts: Principal half-period of sqrt(1229) is Q = 1,4,35,35.
The table headed '1296' must be determinant 1297, whose principal cycle is 1,1.

checkable.sympy: binary_quadratic_form_class_group(disc=4*1129) == CyclicGroup(9)  # pseudo-code; use PARI quadclassunit(4*1129) for an actual check
checkable.asserts: The class group of discriminant 4*1129 is cyclic of order 9, as Gauss's labels 0.9 ... 4.5 imply. The same check with 4*1297 should give order 11 and with 4*1229 order 3.

transcription_corrections: The heading '1296.' is as written in the image, but the table belongs to determinant 1297.

'23.7.' at the bottom left is a separate boxed marginal note (cf. '22.3' on the previous page), not part of the 1296/1297 cycles. The rows '16.13.21.16 . . . 4.7' and '32.21.48.7.39.32 . . . 5.6' at the top of the right column continue the 1297 table.
1433: the bracketed '[-8-]' is a crossed-out stray mark before '&c', not part of the sequence.
